statement.p: Find the solution {\bf r\it(t)} of the differential equation with the given initial condition:

static.solution:
\bf r\it'(t) to find the general solution:
\bf r\it(t)=\int \left\lt \sin 6 t,\sin 6 t,7 t\right> \,dt
= \left\lt \int \sin 6 t dt,\int \sin 6 t dt,\int 7 t dt\right> = \left\lt -\frac{1}{6}\cos 6 t,-\frac{1}{6}\cos 6 t,\frac{7}{2} t^2\right> + \bf c\it Substituting the initial condition we obtain:
\bf r\it(0)=\left\lt -\frac{1}{6}\cos 0,-\frac{1}{6}\cos 0,\frac{7}{2} 0^2\right> + \bf c\it
= \left\lt 3,7,7\right> = \left\lt -\frac{1}{6},-\frac{1}{6},0\right> + \bf c\it Hence,
\bf c\it=\left\lt 3,7,7\right> - \left\lt -\frac{1}{6},-\frac{1}{6},0\right> = \left\lt \frac{19}{6},\frac{43}{6},7\right> Hence the solution to the differential equation with the given initial condition is:
\bf r\it(t)=\left\lt -\frac{1}{6}\cos 6 t,-\frac{1}{6}\cos 6 t,\frac{7}{2} t^2\right> + \left\lt \frac{19}{6},\frac{43}{6},7\right>
=\left\lt \frac{1}{6}\left(19-\cos 6 t\right), \frac{1}{6}\left(43-\cos 6 t\right), 7+\frac{7}{2} t^2\right>
